title: Kernels, images, generated ideals and quotients of quasi-coherent algebras are quasi-coherent, computed on affine opens
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. A *quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebra* is a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras whose underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. (a) Let $\psi:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ be a morphism of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebras. Then the kernel $\mathcal J=\ker\psi$ ($U\mapsto\ker\psi_U$) is a sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal B$ which is quasi-coherent, the image $\operatorname{Im}\psi\subseteq\mathcal A$ (the subsheaf of local sections of $\mathcal A$ which are locally in the image of $\psi$) is a sub-$\mathcal O_X$-algebra of $\mathcal A$ which is quasi-coherent, and for every affine open $U\subseteq X$: $\mathcal J(U)=\ker(\psi_U)$ and $(\operatorname{Im}\psi)(U)=\psi_U(\mathcal B(U))$. (b) Let $\mathcal B$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebra, $\mathcal E$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module and $e:\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$ an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map. Let $(e(\mathcal E))\subseteq\mathcal B$ be the sheaf of ideals generated by $e(\mathcal E)$ (the smallest sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal B$ containing $e_U(\mathcal E(U))$ for all open $U$; it is the image of the $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$, $b\otimes s\mapsto b\,e(s)$). Then $(e(\mathcal E))$ is quasi-coherent, and for every affine open $U$, $(e(\mathcal E))(U)$ is the ideal of $\mathcal B(U)$ generated by $e_U(\mathcal E(U))$. The quotient $\mathcal B/(e(\mathcal E))$ (sheafification of $U\mapsto\mathcal B(U)/(e(\mathcal E))(U)$) is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebra with a surjective algebra map $q:\mathcal B\to\mathcal B/(e(\mathcal E))$ such that for every affine open $U$ the map $q_U$ is surjective with kernel $(e(\mathcal E))(U)$, i.e. $(\mathcal B/(e(\mathcal E)))(U)=\mathcal B(U)/(e(\mathcal E))(U)$; and for every morphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-algebras $\chi:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ with $\chi\circ e=0$ there is exactly one algebra map $\bar\chi:\mathcal B/(e(\mathcal E))\to\mathcal C$ with $\bar\chi\circ q=\chi$.

proof.text: *Step 0 (conventions; affine opens).* A sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras is a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal B$ with a morphism of sheaves of rings $\sigma_{\mathcal B}:\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal B$; its underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] has $r\cdot b=\sigma_{\mathcal B}(r)b$, and a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-algebras is $\mathcal O_X$-linear. Every open $W\subseteq X$ is a union of affine opens contained in $W$: a point $x\in W$ has an open neighbourhood isomorphic to some $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-pc-scheme], and the principal opens $D(f)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$, which are affine ($D(f)\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_f$), form a basis of its topology. Consequently, for a subsheaf $\mathcal K$ of a sheaf $\mathcal B$ and $s\in\mathcal B(W)$: $s\in\mathcal K(W)$ as soon as $s|_V\in\mathcal K(V)$ for all affine opens $V\subseteq W$ (glue the $s|_V$ in $\mathcal K$; the glued section maps to $s$ by the uniqueness in the sheaf $\mathcal B$). This remark is used in Steps 4-6.

source.place: Schemes, Section 01LA (line 4717: the properties of QCoh(O_X) are inherited from the affine case since quasi-coherence is local)

proof.text: *Step 1 ((a), the kernel).* $\psi$ is $\mathcal O_X$-linear (Step 0), so it has a kernel $\mathcal J=\ker\psi$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, computed sectionwise: $\mathcal J(U)=\ker(\psi_U)$ for every open $U$, in particular for affine $U$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Each $\psi_U$ is a ring homomorphism, so $\ker\psi_U$ is an ideal of $\mathcal B(U)$, and restriction maps of $\mathcal B$ carry $\mathcal J(U)$ into $\mathcal J(V)$: $\mathcal J$ is a sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal B$. As $\mathcal B,\mathcal A$ are quasi-coherent, $\mathcal J$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel].

*Step 2 ((a), the image).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] to the $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\psi:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ between quasi-coherent modules: the subsheaf $\operatorname{Im}\psi\subseteq\mathcal A$ of local sections locally in the image of $\psi$ (the subsheaf named in the statement) is a quasi-coherent sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module of $\mathcal A$ with $(\operatorname{Im}\psi)(U)=\psi_U(\mathcal B(U))$ for every affine open $U$. It is a sub-$\mathcal O_X$-algebra: $1=\psi_W(1)$ and $\sigma_{\mathcal A}(r)=\psi_W(\sigma_{\mathcal B}(r))$ lie in it; if $s,t\in(\operatorname{Im}\psi)(W)$, each point of $W$ has a neighbourhood $V$ (the intersection of the two neighbourhoods given by the definition, restricting the preimages) with $s|_V=\psi_V(b)$, $t|_V=\psi_V(c)$, hence $(st)|_V=\psi_V(bc)$ and $(s-t)|_V=\psi_V(b-c)$, so $st,s-t\in(\operatorname{Im}\psi)(W)$.

*Step 3 ((b), the ideal $\mathcal I=(e(\mathcal E))$ as an image).* Let $\mathcal T=\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal E$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], the sheafification of the presheaf $\mathcal T_p:U\mapsto\mathcal B(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X(U)}\mathcal E(U)$, with sheafification map $t:\mathcal T_p\to\mathcal T$. For each open $U$ the map $\mathcal B(U)\times\mathcal E(U)\to\mathcal B(U)$, $(b,s)\mapsto b\,e_U(s)$, is $\mathcal O_X(U)$-bilinear ($e_U$ is $\mathcal O_X(U)$-linear), so it induces an $\mathcal O_X(U)$-linear $\mu^p_U:\mathcal T_p(U)\to\mathcal B(U)$, $b\otimes s\mapsto b\,e_U(s)$; these commute with restrictions ($e$ and the restrictions of $\mathcal B$ are compatible with restriction and multiplicative), so $\mu^p$ is a morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules into the sheaf $\mathcal B$, and by the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] there is a unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\mu:\mathcal T\to\mathcal B$ with $\mu\circ t=\mu^p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections] $\mathcal T$ is quasi-coherent and $t_U$ is bijective for affine $U$. Put $\mathcal I:=\operatorname{Im}\mu\subseteq\mathcal B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] applied to $\mu$, $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module of $\mathcal B$, and for affine $U$: $\mathcal I(U)=\mu_U(\mathcal T(U))=\mu^p_U(\mathcal B(U)\otimes\mathcal E(U))=\{\sum_i b_ie_U(s_i)\}$, which is the ideal of $\mathcal B(U)$ generated by $e_U(\mathcal E(U))$.

proof.text: *Step 4 ((b), $\mathcal I$ is the sheaf of ideals generated by $e(\mathcal E)$).* (i) $\mathcal I$ is a sheaf of ideals: for $x\in\mathcal I(W)$, $c\in\mathcal B(W)$ and any affine open $V\subseteq W$, $x|_V\in\mathcal I(V)$, an ideal of $\mathcal B(V)$ by Step 3, so $(cx)|_V=c|_Vx|_V\in\mathcal I(V)$; by Step 0, $cx\in\mathcal I(W)$. (ii) $e_W(\mathcal E(W))\subseteq\mathcal I(W)$ for every open $W$: for $s\in\mathcal E(W)$ and affine $V\subseteq W$, $e_W(s)|_V=e_V(s|_V)\in\mathcal I(V)$ (Step 3); apply Step 0. (iii) Minimality: if $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal B$ is a sheaf of ideals with $e_U(\mathcal E(U))\subseteq\mathcal K(U)$ for all $U$, then for affine $V$, $\mathcal I(V)$ is the ideal generated by $e_V(\mathcal E(V))$, hence $\subseteq\mathcal K(V)$; for $x\in\mathcal I(W)$ all $x|_V$ ($V\subseteq W$ affine) lie in $\mathcal K(V)$, so $x\in\mathcal K(W)$ by Step 0. Hence $\mathcal I=(e(\mathcal E))$ is the smallest sheaf of ideals containing all $e_U(\mathcal E(U))$, it is the image of $\mathcal B\otimes\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$, quasi-coherent, with the affine sections of Step 3.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 05JS (lines 3320-3335: 'the ideal generated by the image of E'); written out by the agent from Steps 0 and 3

proof.text: *Step 5 ((b), the quotient algebra).* By Step 4 each $\mathcal I(U)$ is an ideal of $\mathcal B(U)$, so $\mathcal P:U\mapsto\mathcal B(U)/\mathcal I(U)$ (restrictions induced by those of $\mathcal B$) is a presheaf of commutative rings with the quotient maps $p:\mathcal B\to\mathcal P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheafification-space-underlying-abelian](1) it has a sheafification $\theta:\mathcal P\to\mathcal Q=\mathcal P^\#$ as a presheaf of commutative rings; $\mathcal Q$ with $\sigma_{\mathcal Q}=\theta p\sigma_{\mathcal B}$ is a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras and $q:=\theta\circ p:\mathcal B\to\mathcal Q$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-algebras; this $\mathcal Q$ is $\mathcal B/(e(\mathcal E))$ of the statement. Let $\iota:\mathcal I\to\mathcal B$ be the inclusion and $q_C:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C=\operatorname{Coker}\iota$ its cokernel in the abelian category $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Since $\mathcal I,\mathcal B$ are quasi-coherent (Step 3), [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] applied to $\iota$ (whose image is $\mathcal I$) gives: $\mathcal C$ is quasi-coherent, $q_C$ is an epimorphism with $q_C\iota=0$, and for affine $U$, $q_{C,U}$ is surjective with kernel $\mathcal I(U)$. Compare $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal Q$. (i) $q$ is $\mathcal O_X$-linear (Step 0) and kills $\mathcal I$ ($p$ does), so by the universal property of the cokernel there is a unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear $h:\mathcal C\to\mathcal Q$ with $hq_C=q$. (ii) The maps $\mathcal P(U)\to\mathcal C(U)$, $p_U(b)\mapsto q_{C,U}(b)$, are well defined additive maps ($q_{C,U}$ kills $\mathcal I(U)$) compatible with restrictions, a morphism of abelian presheaves from $\mathcal P$ to the abelian sheaf $\mathcal C$; by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheafification-space-underlying-abelian](2) ($\theta$ is also the abelian sheafification of $\mathcal P$) there is a unique morphism of abelian sheaves $g:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal C$ with $g\theta p=q_C$, i.e. $gq=q_C$. (iii) $ghq_C=gq=q_C$, and $q_{C,V}$ is surjective for every affine open $V$, so $gh$ and $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$ agree on sections over affine opens and hence everywhere (Step 0): $gh=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$; $hg\theta p=hq_C=q=\theta p$ and every $p_U$ is surjective, so $hg\theta=\theta$, whence $hg=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal Q}$ by the uniqueness in (2). So $h$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules: $\mathcal Q$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebra, $q=hq_C$ is surjective (an epimorphism), and for affine $U$, $q_U$ is surjective with kernel $\mathcal I(U)$, i.e. $\mathcal Q(U)=\mathcal B(U)/\mathcal I(U)$.

proof.text: *Step 6 ((b), universal property).* Let $\chi:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C'$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras with $\chi\circ e=0$. Its sectionwise kernel $U\mapsto\ker\chi_U$ is a sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal B$ (as in Step 1, [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]) containing every $e_U(\mathcal E(U))$, so it contains $\mathcal I$ by Step 4(iii): $\chi_U(\mathcal I(U))=0$ for all $U$. Hence the $\chi_U$ induce ring maps $\bar\chi^p_U:\mathcal P(U)\to\mathcal C'(U)$ with $\bar\chi^p_Up_U=\chi_U$, compatible with restrictions: a morphism of presheaves of commutative rings $\mathcal P\to\mathcal C'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheafification-space-underlying-abelian](1) there is exactly one morphism of sheaves of rings $\bar\chi:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal C'$ with $\bar\chi\theta=\bar\chi^p$; then $\bar\chi q=\bar\chi^pp=\chi$, and $\bar\chi\sigma_{\mathcal Q}=\chi\sigma_{\mathcal B}=\sigma_{\mathcal C'}$, so $\bar\chi$ is a map of $\mathcal O_X$-algebras. Uniqueness: if $\chi'$ is an algebra map with $\chi'q=\chi$, then $\chi'\theta p=\bar\chi\theta p$, and $p_U$ is surjective for every $U$, so $\chi'\theta=\bar\chi\theta$ and $\chi'=\bar\chi$ by the uniqueness in the sheafification property.

split_report.summary: Split into the module-level Stacks results plus algebra bookkeeping. Module level: kernel quasi-coherent (new lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel, Schemes 01IC/01LB; stated exactly by the sorry-free slopmaster2 declaration AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isQuasicoherent_kernel), cokernel and image quasi-coherent with sections over affines (new lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image, 01IC/01IB/01LA(5)), tensor product quasi-coherent with affine sections the tensor of sections (new lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections, 01I8(1)/01CE). Algebra level: kernel is a sheaf of ideals (sectionwise), image a subalgebra (local sections), the ideal (e(E)) = Im(B (x) E -> B) with its minimality checked on affine opens (Step 0: affine opens cover every open), the quotient algebra as ring sheafification of B(U)/I(U) identified with the module cokernel by the two universal properties (existing lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheafification-space-underlying-abelian), universal property from the ring sheafification. Statement kept; stmt_deps gained def-weil-pbc-sheafification and def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, which the statement uses. lean.statement: theorem kernel_image_quasiCoherent {X : Scheme.{u}} (B A : X.CommAlgebraSheaf) (hB : B.toModule.IsQuasicoherent) (hA : A.toModule.IsQuasicoherent) (ψ : B ⟶ A) : (∃ (J : X.Modules) (i : J ⟶ B.toModule), J.IsQuasicoherent ∧ ∀ U : X.Opens, Function.Injective (i.app U) ∧ Set.range (i.app U) = (RingHom.ker (ψ.right.hom.app (op U)).hom : Set (B.right.obj.obj (op U)))) ∧ (∃ (D : X.CommAlgebraSheaf) (k : D ⟶ A), D.toModule.IsQuasicoherent ∧ (∀ U : X.Opens, Function.Injective (k.right.hom.app (op U))) ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens) (s : A.right.obj.obj (op U)), s ∈ Set.range (k.right.hom.app (op U)) ↔ ∀ x : X, x ∈ U → ∃ (V : X.Opens) (hVU : V ≤ U), x ∈ V ∧ A.right.obj.map (homOfLE hVU).op s ∈ Set.range (ψ.right.hom.app (op V))) ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen U → Set.range (k.right.hom.app (op U)) = Set.range (ψ.right.hom.app (op U))))
lean.note: Part (a) is kernel_image_quasiCoherent; part (b) is generated_ideal_quotient_quasiCoherent. Ideals are represented by module-sheaf inclusions with injective section maps and specified ideal ranges; no additional definition is introduced. Quotient presheaf sections are specified by surjectivity and kernel, and the quotient sheaf and its map are tied to the existing sheafification adjunction unit.
